S59.01.needs: a signed-in account that can use tools
S59.01.note: The quoted code lines in the plan are stale; the buttons are built in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/CloudToolApprovalControls.tsx.
steps: Sign in and open a chat that can use tools (AGI Cloud).
Set Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals to Ask before every action.
Ask the agent for an action that needs approval, for example a write.
Tap Allow once on that one card.
Look: only that call runs, and the reply continues with its result.
S59.01.where: Chat > the tool call card in the transcript > Allow once or Deny

S59.02.needs: a Cloud task run paused for approval with several pending calls
S59.02.note: Deny is applied to all pending calls in the same way; the tab is labelled AGI Work, not Tasks.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Work (shown only when cloud tasks are on).
Open a run that has Waiting for your approval.
Read the listed tool calls in that section.
Tap Approve (it approves every pending call of that run at once).
Look: the run continues and the pending calls are no longer listed as waiting.
S59.02.where: Drawer > AGI Work > open a run labelled Waiting for your approval > Approve

S59.03.needs: a Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
S59.03.note: The button appears only when the server offers the session scope for that tool.
steps: Open a chat with tools and trigger an approval for a tool.
Tap Allow for this chat on the card.
If the tool is marked destructive, confirm in the dialog that opens.
Ask the agent to use the same tool again in the same chat.
Look: the second call runs without a new card asking first.
S59.03.where: Chat > the tool call card > Allow for this chat

S59.04.needs: a Cloud account with a connected app
S59.04.note: Code shows allow/ask/block per tool only; no single app-wide setting was found. Unset tools follow Action approvals.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Cloud group, then tap Connectors.
Open a connected app.
Under Tool permissions, find a tool and read its Policy row.
Tap Allow, Ask or Block on that tool.
Look: the row shows the new choice, and the tool follows it on its next run.
S59.04.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > open a connector > Tool permissions

S59.07.needs: a signed-in Cloud account; a second device for the cross-device check
S59.07.note: The sync code is in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/tool-approvals/useToolApprovalPolicySync; I did not read its storage details, so cross-device persistence is unverified.
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Choose Run read-only actions without asking.
Close the screen, force-quit the app and open it again.
Open Action approvals again.
Look: the same choice is still selected. Repeat on a second signed-in device if you have one.

S59.08.note: Skip approvals is disabled when the workspace blocks it. The short composer labels (Ask, Auto, Skip) are defined in the same file, but I did not find the composer control.
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Read the three choices: Ask before every action, Run read-only actions without asking, Skip approvals.
Tap each choice in turn; a Recommended tag sits on Ask before every action.
Look: the selected choice moves, and the Safety default card below updates to match.

labels.text: Reads, searches, page fetches and sandboxed code run on their own; writes still ask.

S59.10.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that reads and one that writes
S59.10.note: No separate mode with this name exists; the behaviour is the middle option of the same selector.
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Tap Run read-only actions without asking.
In a chat, ask the agent to search or read something, then to write or send something.
Look: the read runs with no card; the write stops at an approval card.
S59.10.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Run read-only actions without asking

S59.11.note: Same control as S59.10; the risk split comes from the server review.
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Tap Run read-only actions without asking.
In a chat, ask for a search or page read, then for a riskier action such as a delete or a purchase.
Look: the search runs by itself; the riskier action shows a card and waits.
S59.11.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Run read-only actions without asking

S59.12.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
S59.12.note: The risk label text comes from TOOL_APPROVAL_RISK_LABELS, which I did not locate in packages, so the exact wording is unverified.
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Read the card: the tool summary line, the risk label, and the parameter rows.
Check any notice (for example the private-data notice for high risk).
Look: the card says what the tool will do and why it asks.
S59.12.where: Chat > the tool call card (above the Allow once and Deny buttons)

S59.13.needs: a signed-in account with a send tool that needs approval
S59.13.note: Row names come from the argument key (humanised), not a fixed string; the recipient key list is in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-stakes.ts.
steps: Ask the agent to send an email or message that needs approval.
Read the card before tapping anything.
Find the row for recipients (To, Cc, Bcc, channel or attendees).
Look: the exact address or name appears above Allow once.
S59.13.where: Chat > the approval card for a send (email, message or invite) > read the To row above Allow once

S59.14.needs: a signed-in account with a tool that reaches an outside service
S59.14.note: The destination is shown as a parameter row, not as a dedicated label; the stakes code was not fully traced.
steps: Ask the agent for an action that sends data to a web address or service.
Read the parameter rows on the card, in monospace.
Find the url, host or target row.
Look: the exact destination is shown before you tap Allow once.
S59.14.where: Chat > the approval card for an outbound action > read the parameter rows above Allow once

S59.15.needs: a signed-in account with a payment tool that needs approval
S59.15.note: Amount and item rows come from argument keys in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-stakes.ts; the exact wording depends on the tool.
steps: Ask the agent for a purchase or payment that needs approval.
Read the card before tapping anything.
Find the amount row (for example Amount) and the item row.
Look: the exact amount and what is bought are shown before approval.
S59.15.where: Chat > the approval card for a payment or purchase > read the amount row above Allow once

S59.16.needs: a signed-in account with a command or code tool that needs approval
S59.16.note: Where the command runs is not shown as its own row; only the arguments are shown.
steps: Ask the agent to run a command that needs approval.
Read the parameter rows on the card (monospace text).
Open Raw JSON to see the full arguments.
Look: the exact command line is shown before Allow once.
S59.16.where: Chat > the approval card for a command > read the parameter rows above Allow once

S59.17.needs: a signed-in account with a write tool that needs approval
S59.17.note: Records are shown as argument rows; there is no dedicated list of affected records in the code I read.
steps: Ask the agent to change or create files or records that needs approval.
Read the path and item rows on the card.
Open Raw JSON if you need the full arguments.
Look: the exact file or record names are shown before approval.
S59.17.where: Chat > the approval card for a write > read the parameter rows and any stakes above Allow once

S59.18.needs: a signed-in account with a file edit tool that needs approval
S59.18.note: The diff shows only when the arguments include a before and after shape (detectFileDiff); it is drawn by apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ToolFileDiffBlock.tsx.
steps: Ask the agent to edit a file that needs approval.
Look at the card before tapping anything.
Read the proposed diff block (removed and added lines).
Look: the proposed change is visible before you tap Allow once.
S59.18.where: Chat > the approval card for a file edit > the diff block above Allow once

S59.19.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Allow once.
Look: the card changes to Allowed and the tool runs; the result appears in the transcript.
S59.19.where: Chat > the approval card > Allow once

S59.20.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
S59.20.note: The model's reply to a denial was not verified from code.
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Deny.
Look: the card shows Denied, the action does not run, and the agent replies that it was refused.

labels.text: Tell the agent what to do instead

S59.22.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a tool that asks for approval
S59.22.note: The agent's continuation after guidance is not verified from the code I read.
steps: Ask the agent for an action that needs approval.
Tap Add guidance under the card.
Type what to do instead, for example Use the draft folder.
Tap Deny (or Allow once) to send it.
Look: the guidance is sent with the decision and the agent continues from it.
S59.22.where: Chat > the approval card > Add guidance > type in the box > Allow once or Deny

labels.text: This approval request expired or is no longer active.

S59.23.needs: a pending approval that is left unanswered
S59.23.note: I did not find a fixed time limit in the code read; expiry looks tied to the turn no longer being live (isApprovalTurnLive in stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts). Unverified.
steps: Leave an approval card unanswered in a chat for a long time, or let the run pause or end.
Reopen the chat.
Look: the card shows an expired line and its Allow and Deny buttons are not usable.
S59.23.where: No control: a pending approval that is no longer live shows an expired line in the chat

S59.24.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with past approvals
S59.24.note: The section is hidden in local-only mode, and it shows a retry message when it fails to load.
steps: Open Settings, tap Capabilities, then tap Action approvals.
Scroll to Approval history.
Tap an earlier entry if the list offers it.
Look: past requests appear with their decisions.
S59.24.where: Settings > Capabilities > Action approvals > Approval history

labels.text: Unset tools follow your Action approvals setting.

S59.25.needs: a Cloud account with a connector tool set to Allow or an always-allow grant
S59.25.note: The reset control's visible text was not found; only its accessibility label Reset <tool> to default was. Folder or site grants were not found in mobile code.
steps: Open Settings, go to Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Open a connector that has a tool set to Allow.
Under Tool permissions, find the tool and tap its reset control (labelled Reset to default).
Ask the agent to use that tool in a chat.
Look: the approval card asks again.
S59.25.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > open a connector > Tool permissions > reset a tool

S59.26.needs: two signed-in devices on the same account and a paused task
S59.26.note: The result on device A depends on a server refresh; I did not confirm the refresh path, so the first-device update is unverified.
steps: Start a task that pauses for approval on device A.
Sign in to the same account on device B and open AGI Work.
Open the same run and tap Approve.
Look: device A shows the run moving on and the decision recorded.
S59.26.where: Drawer > AGI Work > open a run labelled Waiting for your approval > Approve (on a second device)

labels.text: This tool can change or delete data, and its effect may not be reversible.

S59.28.needs: a signed-in account with a destructive tool that asks for approval
S59.28.note: The code shows a confirmation dialog for destructive tools; it does not remove the permanent option or force a re-ask. The high-risk private-data notice is in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts.
steps: Ask the agent to run a destructive tool (a delete or change that cannot be undone).
Tap Always allow or Allow for this chat on the card.
Read the dialog title and message; it has Cancel and a confirm button.
Look: the dialog warns before the permission is saved; Cancel leaves the tool asking.
S59.28.where: Chat > the approval card for a destructive tool > Always allow or Allow for this chat > confirmation dialog

S59.30.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with a multi-step task that asks for approval
S59.30.note: Resume behaviour is in apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts; I did not trace it fully.
steps: Ask the agent for a multi-step task that includes one approval.
Tap Allow once on that card.
Look: the same assistant reply continues below the card, without starting a new message.
S59.30.where: No control of its own: the same chat message continues after Allow once, Deny or Add guidance

S59.31.needs: a signed-in Cloud account with two approval requests
S59.31.note: The outcome text after a run was not traced in detail.
steps: Approve one action with Allow once and deny another with Deny.
Look at each card after the decision.
Read the decided label (Allowed or Denied) and the result or outcome line below it.
S59.31.where: Chat > the approval card after a decision (the transcript row keeps the decision)
